newsitem.title: USA: Fair weather forecasted for U.S. corp bond supply.
newsitem.headline: Fair weather forecasted for U.S. corp bond supply.

text.p: Expectations were high for continued strong issuance of both high-yield and investment-grade corporate bond issuance for the near future, market sources said.
"Things won't slow down until the last week in August," said one junk bond syndicate official, adding the forward calendar for junk bonds had grown to around $4 billion.
AMG Data Services reported healthy net cash inflows of $389 million into junk bond mutual funds for the latest week, confirming that strong technicals continue to support the new issue boom.

"Between new (collaterlized bond obligations) and pension fund allocations, this number has become less and less meaningful," said a junk bond player, who noted the investor base for junk bonds continues to expand.
"You notice we priced $4 billion in new deals last week and only had $400 million in (mutual fund) inflows," he pointed out.
While the typically sleepy month of August is proving to be a busy month for new issues, activity for this Friday is nevertheless expected to be slow, players said.
On today's agenda, Atlas Air Inc, an air cargo carrier, is expected to sell $100 million in eight-year notes in a 144a private placement via BT Securities Corp.
Price talk for the B3/B-minus-rated deal is around 10.25 percent, sources said.
First out of the chute next week may be Las Vegas-casino operator, Riviera Holdings Corp, with a $155 million deal. Jefferies & Co Inc will be the underwriter.
On Friday, Moody's Investors Service rated the company's proposed offering B1 and said it may increase the B1 rating of its outstanding first mortgage notes.
IXC Communications Inc is also preparing an offering of $200 million in junior exchangeable preferred stock via Credit Suisse First Boston which could arrive early next week.

In high-grades, Raytheon Co's $3.0 billion mega-debt offering from Thursday was heard well-bid in the secondary market. Spreads on Raytheon's 30-year debt tranche tightened to 73-73 basis points on Friday after being priced at 75 basis points, according to one trader.
Elsewhere, Apache Corp priced $150 million in debentures (Baa1/BBB-plus) at a spread of 88 basis points via Goldman Sachs & Co on Friday.
